items.t: XPeng's Korea Leadership Hire and Robotaxi Green Light Add Weight to October's 50,237-Vehicle Record
sum: XPeng shares climbed 7.2% on Thursday, recovering alongside a broader rebound in electric-vehicle and growth stocks as investors returned to the sector following two sessions of selling in the wake of the US midterm elections. Yet the more durable story for the Chinese automaker sits beneath the market mood, in a pair of operational developments that give the rally something concrete to stand on.

The stock's advance came as media reports described renewed appetite for growth names after the post-election pullback. For XPeng, that tailwind arrives at a useful moment: the company has fresh delivery momentum and an overseas expansion taking shape, and both will be measured against hard financial results before long.

XPeng reported 50,237 vehicles delivered in October, a monthly record. The figure represented a 22% increase over the prior month and a 20% gain year-on-year. The combination of sequential acceleration and annual growth carries more weight than the record label alone, pointing to genuine demand momentum — provided the company can convert higher volumes into economically sound expansion.

Deliveries outside China also reached a monthly record, with 13,326 vehicles handed over, up 166% from a year earlier. That sharp growth underpins the case for XPeng's international strategy, though the financial quality of that expansion will only become clear in the coming results.

On Tuesday, XPeng announced the appointment of Lee Man-sik as managing director of XPENG Motors Korea, effective December 1, 2026, as the company prepares to enter the South Korean market. A named leadership role gives the project organizational shape and signals a structured approach to international growth. Whether the move proves economically convincing will depend on execution down the line.

Beyond vehicle sales, XPeng received approval on October 26 for Level-4 robotaxi demonstration operations in Guangzhou. According to the company, the program now advances to testing under real operating conditions and to validation of the business model. The permit matters because it enables a practical test: the autonomous-driving narrative gains a concrete operational anchor, contingent on the technology and business model proving themselves in the field.

XPENG had a fantabulous sales month in October. We can give you the numbers, but as you can see well enough in the chart above and below, the company’s sales soared to a whole new level last month.

Reaching 50,237 vehicle deliveries, that meant 22% sales growth month over month and 20% sales growth year over year. Will it be another year until XPENG beats its monthly sales record again, or is the October 2026 result just the beginning of more record sales in coming months?

A big portion of this sales growth came from tremendous growth in sales outside of XPENG’s home market of China. “Overseas deliveries also reached an all-time monthly high of 13,326 units, up 166% year-over-year,” the company shares.

XPENG is a China-based technology company focused on designing, developing, manufacturing, and marketing smart electric vehicles. The company combines electric powertrain technology with software, connectivity, and advanced driver-assistance features to create vehicles built for digitally connected and increasingly automated transportation. Its lineup includes electric sedans, sport utility vehicles, and multipurpose vans aimed at tech-savvy drivers. As a fast-growing consumer stock, XPENG competes in the worlds largest electric vehicle market, where innovation, pricing, and software capabilities increasingly determine which brands stand out among a crowded field of domestic and international rivals.

Shares fell to a new yearly low during the latest session, extending a decline that has weighed on the stock for months. sum: During the U.S. trading session on October 21, SpaceX shares surged more than 12% intraday, pushing its total market value to $2.25 trillion and briefly overtaking TSMC, making it the day's most closely watched focus. At the same time, popular Chinese ADRs weakened collectively, with the Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index falling more than 3% intraday—a sharp contrast to the broad gains among large-cap tech stocks.

SpaceX shares hit an intraday high of $165.641, the biggest single-day gain since August, and were still up more than 9% as of press time. On the news front, the company's third-quarter revenue reached $14.6 billion, up 161% year-over-year. Elon Musk said that, based on current trends, annual recurring revenue (ARR) could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027. That guidance significantly exceeded market expectations and was the direct trigger for the stock's sharp rally.

Space-concept stocks rose broadly in response. Rocket Lab gained 2.79%, Planet Labs 3.21%, AST SpaceMobile 1.54% and Intuitive Machines 3.70%. The semiconductor sector also advanced mostly, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up more than 1%; memory-chip names Seagate Technology and Western Digital rose more than 2%, and South Korea's SK Hynix gained more than 1%. Optical communications names were active: Lumentum rose 5.97%, Coherent 4.24%, Applied Optoelectronics 4.69%, Ciena 5.46% and Marvell Technology 3.27%.

AI server makers emerged as another main thread. Super Micro Computer shares rose 12%, the biggest gain in two months. The company preliminarily estimated first-quarter net sales at $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, far above market expectations; it also announced a partnership with Nokia to deploy Nvidia's Aerial RAN computing solution at the network edge to support low-latency AI services. Dell Technologies rose more than 7% and Hewlett Packard Enterprise more than 4%.

Large-cap tech stocks were mixed. Tesla rose more than 3%, Meta and Nvidia more than 2%, and Apple 0.46%; Google fell more than 2%, Amazon more than 1%, and Microsoft edged lower. Netflix dropped more than 6% to a more than two-year low; the company expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $13.44 billion, below analysts' estimate of $13.51 billion.

sum: XPeng Motors (09868.HK) dropped a major strategic announcement during the Paris Motor Show, revealing plans to open its smart vehicle technology to global partners, offering one-stop technology solutions spanning complete vehicle R&D, production, and after-sales services. Group Chairman and CEO He Xiaopeng personally attended the Paris Automotive Summit to formally introduce the "XPENG AI ENGINEERING" smart vehicle solutions business, while also disclosing the company's European ambitions: targeting annual sales of 500,000 vehicles in Europe by the end of 2030.

He Xiaopeng stated at the summit that XPeng will open not only automotive technology but also full-spectrum physical AI ecosystem solutions, including humanoid robots, Robotaxi, flying cars, the Turing AI chip, and physical world foundation models. "The Group not only shares technology with partners but grows together with them, fully supporting partners in mastering relevant technologies and carrying out innovative work," he said. He also welcomed global partners to join, enabling mutual learning, technology exchange, and collaborative progress.

In terms of the technology licensing scope, XPeng's open smart vehicle commercialization solutions encompass three core pillars. First is complete vehicle platform architecture, including the vehicle platform and electronic/electrical architecture. Second is modular technology, covering key components such as intelligent driving, AI BOX, chips, batteries, and electric drive systems. Third is the full toolchain, including remote XCP calibration, end-of-line (EOL) testing, and AI diagnostics for complete after-sales and development support.

Capital markets responded positively to the news. During afternoon trading in Hong Kong, XPeng shares rose more than 3% at one point, trading at HK$38.8 (approximately $4.9) as of press time, up 2.54%, with turnover reaching HK$217 million (approximately $27.7 million).

sum: China, June 29, 2026 — XPENG (NYSE: XPEV, HKEX: 9868), a leading China-based high-tech company, shared key insights at the CVPR 2026 Workshop on Foundation Model Deployment for Embodied Intelligence, hosted in Denver, U.S. this June. He proposed that proactive reasoning, controllable generation, and long-horizon forecasting are three indispensable capabilities for a high-performance World Model, the core prerequisites for deploying World Models in the field of autonomous driving.

In the first half of this year, XPENG's R&D team published a suite of world-model-focused academic reports, including X-World, X-Foresight, and X-Cache, which systematically disassembled R&D methodologies around controllable generation and long-horizon forecasting. Recently, addressing the critical challenge of enabling models to think proactively and pushing the upper limit of predictive performance, XPENG Group officially released the X-Mind technical framework. By embedding a predictive World Model, X-Mind endows vehicle-side agents with an efficient visual Chain-of-Thought, successfully resolving the tension between cognitive reasoning and real-time computation, thereby establishing an entirely new technical paradigm for achieving genuinely safe, human-like autonomous driving.

Traditional mainstream industry solutions remain confined to a reactive mapping stage of "perception-to-action". This is highly analogous to a driver stepping on the accelerator while staring solely at the instantaneous frame directly ahead, lacking any explicit prediction capability regarding the spatial-temporal evolution of the physical world.

Specifically, the notable shortcomings are twofold. First, text-based reasoning struggles to accurately express complex environmental geometry. Second, predicting future raw images introduces a massive amount of high-frequency, redundant textural data, while lacking the deep semantic information that is vital for autonomous driving tasks.
